recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce Definition.category without a new FHIR-I decision revisiting the CanonicalResource/Definition alignment; any new category-like indexing requirement for definitional artifacts should be handled as a fresh issue against the current canonical/metadata pattern model.
issue_request: FHIR-35832 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request asking for guidance on how resource.category should be used. The accepted resolution defined a 0..* unbound CodeableConcept category element for Request, Event, and Definition workflow patterns with guidance on filtering, access control, system behavior, automatic or manual categorization, multiple category axes, and avoiding strong overall bindings; it also asked for Definition guidance distinguishing category from usageContext and jurisdiction.
initial_application: Git commit 193d552d630fe22578c31b120f6db85fefd90a6d explicitly named FHIR-35832 and added Definition.category, Event.category, and Request.category guidance to the workflow pattern spreadsheets. Current source retains the requested Request.category and Event.category rows and comments in active logical-pattern spreadsheets.
additional_context: A later Published/Persuasive FHIR-I issue, FHIR-40406, aligned the Definition pattern documentation with CanonicalResource. Its application commit 1e7ed5c7a6146f8bd69ebfb2169cd9c687d9e34d removed Definition.category while retaining/aligning Definition useContext and jurisdiction semantics. source/fhir.ini confirms request, event, definition, canonicalresource, and metadataresource are active build inputs. FHIR-I Confluence minutes corroborate both decisions, and targeted Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community rationale.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Restoring Definition.category would undo the later FHIR-40406 alignment decision; the current Request and Event pattern guidance already conveys the applicable FHIR-35832 category guidance.
